name: How do I keep a kitchen remodel on budget after opening walls?

mainEntity.name: How do I keep a kitchen remodel on budget when hidden problems are discovered after demolition?
mainEntity.text: How do I keep a kitchen remodel on budget when hidden problems are discovered after demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keeping a kitchen remodel on budget after demolition starts with planning for surprises before work begins. Older homes often reveal hidden issues once walls are opened, so a contingency fund is essential. If a problem appears, the contractor should show photos, explain the repair, and provide a written change order before extra work proceeds. Homeowners can protect the budget by separating true necessities from wish-list upgrades. Safety, structural integrity, plumbing failures, and electrical problems should come first. Cosmetic changes can be reconsidered if the budget gets tight. The fastest way to lose control of costs is to make multiple design changes after construction starts, especially changes involving cabinetry, counters, tile, or appliance placement. It also helps to review allowances early and confirm what materials are actually included. Clear scope, written approvals, and disciplined decision-making are the best tools for preventing budget creep during a remodel.
acceptedAnswer.description: Keep the project on budget by setting a contingency fund, approving changes in writing, and prioritizing repairs that affect safety and function first. Avoid redesigning the kitchen mid-project unless the change solves a real problem or prevents a larger cost later.
